name: Itter
kurzbeschreibung: Village with the famous Schloss Itter – once a prison for French politicians and now a luxury hotel.
title: Itter
metaDescription: Discover Itter in the Brixen Valley: Historic Castle Itter and the 1945 battle, Salvistabahn into SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser, Kraftalm, and the Rose Trail.
beschreibung:
Overview

Itter is situated at an elevation of 703 metres in the Tyrolean lowlands in the district of Kitzbühel, perched upon a sunny plateau at the entrance of the Brixen Valley high above the Inn and Mühl valleys. Nestled at the foot of the panoramic Hohe Salve (1,828 m), this picturesque village is home to around 1,180 residents. Celebrated as an award-winning floral village, Itter charms visitors with its peaceful pastoral atmosphere, traditional hereditary farmsteads, and open green meadows, with historic Castle Itter rising majestically on a rocky knoll above the landscape. Despite its quiet location removed from transit traffic, Itter boasts first-rate leisure amenities: The modern Salvistabahn gondola provides direct access to the SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser – Brixental, one of the largest interconnected ski and hiking arenas in Austria.

History

Archaeological finds confirm human settlements on the plateau dating back to the Bronze and Roman eras, with the name originating from the pre-Roman water name Udria. It was first documented in 902 as Uitaradorf during a property donation to the Bishopric of Regensburg. Castle Itter was erected in the 13th century as a fortress for Regensburg bishops before being acquired by the Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg in 1380, later restored in neo-Gothic style during the 19th century. The castle achieved world-historical renown on May 5, 1945, in the Battle for Castle Itter: Used as a high-profile subcamp of Dachau holding VIP French prisoners, US Army soldiers and anti-Nazi German Wehrmacht troops under Major Josef Gangl joined French captives to defend the castle against the Waffen-SS. The Rococo Parish Church of St. Joseph was built between 1762 and 1764 by master builder Franz de Paula Penz.

Getting There

Itter boasts convenient accessibility. By automobile, drivers travel along the Inntal Motorway A12 to the Wörgl-Ost exit, continuing along the B178 and the B170 Brixental road for just six kilometres straight to Itter. Motorists from Bavaria can travel toll-free via Kufstein-Süd and the B173 Eiberg road. Rail travellers arrive at Wörgl Central Station, a major Austrian railway junction located only seven kilometres away, served by high-speed Railjet, ICE, and Eurocity trains. From Wörgl station, regular regional buses (VVT route 4060) connect directly to Itter village square and the Salvistabahn valley terminal.

Tips

The premier recreational attraction is the Salvistabahn gondola, whisking winter sports enthusiasts and hikers up via the alpine Kraftalm to the summit ridge of Kleine Salve (1,565 m), unlocking over 270 kilometres of pistes in the SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser – Brixental. At the middle station, stroll around the sparkling Kleine Salve reservoir lake reflecting the jagged Wilder Kaiser peaks. In the village, walk the idyllic 1.6-kilometre Rose Path (Rosenweg), bordered by hundreds of fragrant rose bushes offering postcard views of Castle Itter. During warm summer days, the heated public outdoor swimming pool in Itter provides wonderful family relaxation.
